alate: Alate: head brown, paler behind, labrum, antennae and pronotum yellowish brown, abdomen black, ocelli yellowish white. Head, pronotum and forewing scales with rather dense erect bristles. Head outline nearly round, a distinct elongate yellow patch between the ocelli, a crescent-shaped yellow patch faintly visible on the inner side in front of each ocellus; compound eyes oval, ocelli elongate-oval, the distance from the compound eye to the lower margin of the head almost equal to the short diameter of the ocellus. Antennae with 19–20 segments, the third or fourth shorter. Anterior margin of the pronotum a broad shallow concavity, the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle. Wing membrane densely covered with fine hairs, the media and cubitus very weak, the veins indistinct; in the forewing the media arising independently at the humeral suture and close to the cubitus, with a faint three-branched fork at its posterior end, the cubitus with eight branches; in the hindwing the media arising from the base of the radial sector, followed by two faint branches, the cubitus with 8–9 branches.
soldier: Soldier: the shape of the head varies, the elongate-oval form making up about 80 per cent and the round form about 20 per cent; in round individuals the head is slightly shorter but distinctly broader and the postmentum shorter, the remaining characters being very similar in the two. Head and antennae orange-yellow, mandibles reddish brown, thoracic and abdominal tergites pale yellow. The sides of the fontanelle mostly with two bristles each, one bristle between the antenna and the fontanelle; the margin of the pronotum with sparse long bristles, the posterior half of the disc with several short hairs, the bristles of the abdominal tergites longer and denser. Whether elongate-oval or round, the head is widest at the middle, the lateral margins rounded, the posterior margin rounded out. Mandibles rather straight, their tips not distinctly curved; labrum longer than wide, reaching the middle of the mandibles; the aperture not visible in dorsal view, the aperture triangular, narrow above and broad below. Antennae with 15 segments, the 3rd and 4th almost equal or the 3rd shorter and smaller. In the elongate-oval form the waist of the postmentum lies slightly below the middle between the widest part and the posterior margin, whereas in the round form the waist clearly lies at the posterior end. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a distinct median concavity, the posterior margin slightly concave but very indistinctly so.
